content:
our idea of what a "dark age" looks like seems hopelessly marred by survivorship bias. many civilizations/subcultures/genres of media don't exist anymore, and presumably it would be fair to characterize the period right before they wink out of existence as a dark age.

but the only dark ages that make it into the literature — medieval Europe, the slow attrition of LessWrong 1.0, the crash of comics as as a medium in the mid 90s — are the ones preceding something like a golden age. or at least a silver one.

i'm not sure what the base rates are, or how to distinguish between reference classes. we don't hear much from groups that don't exist anymore.
